method:
I have read through usage guides and tutorials for various websites—such as detailed instructions for GitHub and GitLab—as well as information regarding the distinct positioning of these two platforms.
I also kept detailed notes and took photos of the common code references Professor Boyd provided to me.
On Thursday, through drawing and observing the technology around me, I integrated technology with myself to create a picture illustrating my relationship with it.
On Friday, I also practiced some coding; although it wasn't entirely successful, I still gained a lot from the experience.
related_work:
From Shell to Sprites -I understand now that the shell is the underlying logic that executes code—much like an engine.
I reviewed the Creative Web presentation and gained an understanding of the diversity and feasibility of web pages and personal blogs.
This week, I read about the origins of net art—tracing the history and fascinating events that evolved from a simple desire to share art to collaborative online artistic creation—which has deepened my interest in the connection between art and technology.
I also learned that Reese creates his work using a camera obscura; the fact that he can reproduce such magnificent art using only color and form is truly amazing.
conclusion_future_work:
I need to conceptualize the items and outputs for my Project 0, as well as the pixel art approach, and then learn how to integrate the code into the layers. Fortunately, I have no classes on Monday, so I still have time to make my choices and complete the first part of Project 0.
I’m not sure why npm isn't working in my terminal, but I can run `npm install` and `npm run cms` within VS Code to launch and edit this blog.
results_discussion:
I’ve had a lot of pleasant experiences this week. I tidied up my assigned desk and arranged the items I needed. I also drew a picture of my partner, Han Yi; although I’m not the best artist, I created a new portrait for her and hope she likes it. I attended a lecture by Rhys, where I saw many fascinating artworks that have enriched my artistic background for the future.
It’s also worth mentioning that we ate a lot of pizza—all courtesy of the professor. It was fantastic—truly an unforgettable experience.
However, I faced significant challenges setting up NPM and the corresponding runtime environment. Fortunately, Boyd patiently guided us; with his instruction, I researched solutions and eventually resolved the issues. I felt the professor's kindness and passed that goodwill on to my classmates by helping them with their downloads and setups whenever I could. Of course, none of this would have been possible without my great mentor, Professor Boyd; otherwise, I don't think I would have ever figured it all out. I haven't fully grasped the subsequent steps yet, but I hope things go more smoothly in the future. Alice will be guiding us through all nine steps. I bet I won't understand a word she says—she speaks so fast!—but she often steps in to help right when I need it, and I’m very grateful to her. I trust she’ll teach me the rest just as Professor Boyd has.
In our final class on Friday, Boyd told us to get some rest and enjoy the weekend. I suppose I tend to get pretty lazy once the weekend hits—hahaha—but I’ll still choose to take a day off to do what I enjoy and eat the food I love. He also emphasized the importance of having a strong community. Knowing that we’ll all rally to help anyone facing difficulties makes me feel wonderful; we support and help one another like family—like a single unit. Honestly, I’m deeply moved. This is my first time experiencing such a wonderful educational environment; coming to the UK to study was the right choice—I’ve gained both respect and love. I will cherish this time and remember this week.
title: My Amazing Week 1!
introduction: Hello World, hello Southampton—Day 1 of coding, and the first week under the guidance of Professor Boyd.I have started thinking about this week's plan, the topic selection for the initial direction of Project 0, and a rough concept for the final project.Gaining a preliminary understanding of code and experiencing the fundamentals of programming has sparked my interest in learning to code.
